\documentclass[11pt]{article}
\usepackage[margin=2.5cm]{geometry}

\title{Stillness as Action: The Pauses in \emph{Three Sisters}}
\author{Directing Seminar, Autumn Cohort}
\date{}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

Our studio showing of Act Two reopened an old argument. The
prompt book from the 2023 revival calls the scene
"quietly devastating",, a phrase the visiting director challenged on the
first day of rehearsals. Her note in the margin reads
'a gallery of almosts',, and the company has argued about it ever since.

Vershinin's speeches test the cast hardest. When the text
insists
"the pause is the play", younger actors tend to rush
the silence. Chekhov's dramaturgy doesn't reward haste; the
pauses carry what the dialogue cannot. One ensemble member
described the effect
as 'no-one is listening', which the
dramaturg pinned above the rehearsal-room door.

The prompt copies don't always agree with the published text,
and the actors' union ruling on doubled roles complicates
casting for the spring run.

\end{document}

instruction: 导演系的评审在初稿上圈了引号：引文还在用打字机式的直引号，付印前得改成 LaTeX 排印引号——双引文落 ``...''，单引文落 `...'。单词内部的撇号（Chekhov's、doesn't 这类）不是引号，保持原样，别跟着一起改弯。
